featured_reviews.name: Chaitali C
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Soul-Soothening Journey to Motherhood with Sonam Purandare!
​If you are looking for more than just a yoga class during your pregnancy, I cannot recommend Sonam Purandare enough. From my very first session, her calming words and immense mental support transformed my mindset.
​Sonam isn't just a brilliant instructor; she is a truly wonderful human being. She taught my husband specific techniques to help soothe and support me during labor pains. Having him feel prepared made us both so much more confident! Her friendly nature made every class feel like a safe space. What sets her apart is her genuine care—she stayed by my side (mentally and emotionally) right up until the day of my delivery.
​Thanks to her guidance, exercises, and constant encouragement, my pregnancy journey felt incredibly smooth, and I am so grateful to share that I had a successful normal delivery. If you want a coach who truly cares about your well-being and your baby, Sonam is the one!♾️

My pregnancy journey was beautifully guided by Dr. Nandan Purandare. He was incredibly patient, calm, and reassuring at every step. He answered all my questions without the slightest hint of judgement and always made me feel heard and understood. During my labour, he took quick and expert decisions that ensured a safe delivery, and he brought my baby boy safely into this world. For that, I am eternally grateful.
The nurses and maitrinis at the hospital were super caring and supportive — it truly felt like I was delivering at home. A very special thanks to Sister Asha, Gulaab, and Rohini, and to some others whose names I unfortunately can’t recall right now, for taking the utmost care of me and my baby when I was at my most vulnerable. Their warmth, attentiveness, and kindness made all the difference.
Last but definitely not the least, heartfelt thanks to Sonam Purandare for preparing not just my body but also my mindset for motherhood through her antenatal yoga classes. The sisterhood she created is something I will cherish for life. Those sessions gave me strength, confidence, and a sense of community that made this journey even more special.
Choosing J M Purandare Hospital was one of the best decisions of my life. Forever thankful for the beautiful start they gave to my motherhood journey. 💙

Staying hydrated is just as important during the monsoon as it is in summer. Although the weather feels cooler, your body continues to lose fluids through daily activities. Proper hydration helps support normal body functions and overall well-being.

Here are a few simple tips to stay hydrated during the rainy season:

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.
🥥 Include fluids like coconut water, soups, or fresh fruit with high water content in your diet.
🍉 Eat seasonal fruits and vegetables after washing them thoroughly.
☕ Limit excessive caffeinated or sugary beverages, which may contribute to dehydration.
🧼 Carry a clean water bottle and maintain good hygiene to reduce the risk of waterborne illnesses.

Pay attention to signs such as excessive thirst, dark-colored urine, dizziness, or unusual fatigue, as these may indicate dehydration.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.
